properties.title: NRC Report: Oil: Diesel in Uppe near Canton, MO
properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 1067711 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: AMERICAN RIVER TRANSPORTATION CO.
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1067711
Incident Time: 2013-12-05 21:10:00
Nearest City: Canton, MO
Location: UPPER MISSISSIPPI MM 343.2 AT BLOCK 20
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: AMERICAN RIVER TRANSPORTATION CO.
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 40.136837, -91.518494 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 1117 gallon
Report Description
***UPDATE TO REPORT 1067705*** CALLER IS REPORTING THAT THE TOWING VESSEL WAS AUTOMATICALLY TRANSFERRING FUEL FROM THE DAY TANK AND THE FUEL PUMP DID NOT AUTOMATICALLY SHUT OFF. THE PUMP ALARM DID NOT GO OFF AND THE TANK OVERFILL ALARM ALSO FAILED. WHEN THE TANK OVERFLOWED THE OVERFLOW WENT TO THE #2 FUEL TANK. WHEN THE #2 TANK WAS FULL IT OVERFLOWED AND THE FUEL WENT ONTO THE DECK AND INTO THE RIVER. THERE WAS A HIGH LEVEL ALARM ON THE #2 TANK THAT DID NOT GO OFF. THE #2 FUEL TANK CAPACITY IS 22,700 GALLONS. THERE IS A TOTAL OF 1,117 GALLONS OF MATERIAL THAT IS UNACCOUNTED FOR. IT IS UNKNOWN HOW MUCH MATERIAL IN TOTAL WENT INTO THE WATER.

Report DescriptionLOCATION: FINA ANCHORAGE, PORT ARTHUR, TEXAS TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 0345CST / 0845Z TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 0750EST / 1150Z AMPLIFYING INFORMATION: • AT 0345CST/0845Z, A BARGE STRUCK TWO BARGES THAT WERE TIED OFF IN THE ANCHORAGE, CAUSING A TWO-TO-THREE-FOOT GASH THREE FEET BELOW THE MAIN DECK BUT ABOVE THE WATERLINE. • THE BARGE THAT WAS STRUCK WAS CARRYING BENZENE, A HAZARDOUS MATERIAL THAT CAN BE EXTREMELY TOXIC, FLAMMABLE, AND WILL DISSIPATE OVER TIME. • THE DAMAGED BARGE HAS A POTENTIAL TO RELEASE 84,000 GALLONS AND IS CONFIRMED TO BE RELEASING THE MATERIAL. • HARD BOOMS, SOFT BOOMS, AND PADS HAVE BEEN DEPLOYED TO CONTROL THE POLLUTED AREA. • THERE ARE NO REPORTED INJURIES. • WEATHER ON SCENE IS REPORTED AS 2 MPH OFFSHORE, WITH LIGHTNING IN THE VICINITY, MAKING CLEANUP POTENTIALLY CHALLENGING. • THERE IS NOT CURRENTLY MEDIA INTEREST, BUT INTEREST IS EXPECTED AS THE SITUATION PROGRESSES.

Nearest City: Traver, CA
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: IRON PHOSPHATE
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: MAF INDUSTRIES
Skytruth Analysis
CALLER IS REPORTING THAT HE BELIEVES HIS COMPANY MAY BE CONTAMINATING THE LOCAL WATER TABLE. THEY HAVE A PAINT DEPARTMENT OUT BACK WHERE THEY PRESSURE WASH AND CLEAN METAL PARTS PRIOR TO PAINTING THEM. THEY CLEAN THE METAL WITH IRON PHOSPHATE AND A PRODUCT CALLED "POWER CLEAN DEGREASER". THE EMPLOYEES HAVE BEEN LED TO BELIEVE THAT ALL THE RUN OFF FROM THIS CLEANING PROJECT GOES DIRECTLY TO A STORM DRAIN THAT LEADS TO A RECOVERY SYSTEM. ABOUT THREE MONTHS AGO THE MAN HOLE LEADING TO THE "RECOVERY SYSTEM" STARTED BACKING UP, SO THEY HAD TO PUMP OUT THE HOLE AND THAT'S WHEN THEY BEGAN PUMPING UP A DARK BLACK OILY SLUDGE. WHEN THEY BROUGHT THIS TO THE OWNERS ATTENTION HE STATED THAT THEY NEVER INVESTED IN A PROPER RECOVERY SYSTEM. THE CALLER BELIEVES THIS MAY HAVE BEEN GOING ON FOR ABOUT 7 YEARS NOW.

Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: WHATCOM CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (WCWP)
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 48.894275, -122.44306 (Approximated from premise)
Report DescriptionNEEC INCIDENT NOTIFICATION: FECAL COLIFORM EXCEEDANCE THIS REPORT IS TO NOTIFY YOU THAT ON 5/27/26, STAFF WORKING IN WASHINGTON STATE AS PART OF THE WHATCOM CLEAN WATER PROGRAM (WCWP) COLLECTED SAMPLES FROM STREAMS FLOWING FROM BRITISH COLUMBIA INTO WHATCOM COUNTY. THESE SAMPLES WERE ANALYZED AT AN ACCREDITED LAB ON 5/28/26 AND FOUND TO EXCEED WATER QUALITY HEALTH BENCHMARKS FOR FECAL COLIFORM. THE ELEVATED RESULTS WERE DOCUMENTED IN THE JACKMAN DITCH DRAINAGE. SAMPLES WERE COLLECTED AS PART OF ROUTINE MONITORING IN THE PORTAGE BAY WATERSHED. SAMPLES WERE COLLECTED AFTER ~0.25 INCH OF RAIN FELL IN THE REGION IN THE 24 HOURS PRIOR TO SAMPLING. FECAL COLIFORM COUNTS REMAINED ELEVATED ABOUT 2.8 KM DOWNSTREAM IN JACKMAN DITCH AT SITE BEJK-0.2 AT 1,200 CFU/100ML. FECAL COLIFORM RESULTS (CFU/100 ML): SITE ID: JD-1.89 SITE LOCATION: JACKMAN RD DITCH ABOUT 500 FEET SOUTH OF BORDER RESULT: >6,000 SITE ID: BEJK-0.2 SITE LOCATION: JACKMAN RD DITCH ABOUT 1.1 KM NORTH OF BADGER RD RESULT: 1,200

Report Description/// THIS IS A CORRECTION TO NRC REPORT # 1464075 /// CORRECT 'COUNTY' IS IN THE 'BETHEL (CENSUS AREA)' NOT 'ANCHORAGE'. CALLER STATES THAT DUE TO THE 'TYPOON HALONG' THAT OCCURRED ON 12OCT2025, THE FOLLOWING 03 VILLAGES NEAR ANCHORAGE WERE ADVERSELY IMPACTED IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: NIGHTNUTE VILLAGE -LAGOON BROKE AND INUNDATED COMMUNITY WITH BAGS OF HUMAN WASTE. KIPNUK -LAGOON BROKE AND INUNDATED COMMUNITY WITH BAGS OF HUMAN WASTE AND VAST AMOUNTS OF DEBRIS. -MIGRATORY BIRDS ARE CURRENTLY NESTING IN THE CONTAMINATED AREA; UTILIZED AS A RESOURCE IN THE VILLAGE, THE COMMUNITY (AND OTHER WILDLIFE) ARE CONSUMING THE NOW CONTAMINATED EGGS. KWIGILLINGOK - A LARGE SECTION OF THE COMMUNITY HAS SUBSIDED FROM THE EVENT BUT ARE INUNDATED WITH 5 FEET WATER AT EVERY HIGH TIDE. - A PIPE AND HEADER AT THE KWIG FUEL FARM (LOCAL BULK TANK FACILITY) IS NOT SECURED AND ACTIVELY DISCHARGES UNKNOWN AMOUNTS OF DIESEL FUEL/KEROSENE HEATING OIL, THEN SETTLES ON THE LAND AT EVERY LOW TIDE; THIS OCCURS EVERY TIDE CYCLE. -A LARGE SECTION OF HOMES/ THE BOARDWALK HAS ALSO SETTLED ON TOP OF THE AFFECTED PIPELINE. EXACT NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS EVACUATED IS ESTIMATED TO BE AROUND 3,000. CALLER STATES THAT THE DELAY IN REPORTING IS DUE TO THE FACT THAT EVERYTHING FROZE DIRECTLY AFTER THE DISASTER AND ARE CURRENTLY AT A POINT WHERE THE IMPACT HAS BEEN DISCOVERED. /// THIS IS A CORRECTION TO NRC REPORT # 1464075 ///

Medium Affected: AIR

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 32.128611, -90.396667 (Explicit)
Report Description***UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER 1259797*** UPDATE INFORMATION ESTIMATED REPORTABLE QUANTITY INCREASED TO 13,028 PUNDS OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE IN 24 HOURS. 2 WELLS CAPS AND DIVERTED TO FLARES. 2 WELLS KILLED. FLOW REMAINS AT 200 MMCF. INCIDENT SCENE CONTINUES TO BE MONITORED BY LA PD, LA DEQ, LA DEC, RED RIVER OFFICE OF HOMELAND SECURITY. UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER # 1259714 /// UPDATED INFO: PREPARING FLOWLINE AND WELLHEAD FOR CAPPING AND FLARING OF THE WELL. CAP AND FLARE SCHEDULED FOR TUESDAY 01-OCT-2019. QUANTITY WILL POTENTIALLY INCREASE AT THAT TIME. RQ REMAINS THE SAME AT 6514 POUNDS. ***UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER 1259548*** UPDATED INFORMATION IS THAT PREPARING CASING FOR CAP AND FLARE OF BLOW OUT WELL. ONE WELL CAPPED AND DIVERTED TO FLARE. TWO WELLS KILLED. OVERFLOW RATE OF 200 MMCF STAYS THE SAME. ESTIMATED REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF 6514 POUNDS NITROGEN DIOXIDE OVER 24 HOUR PERIOD REMAINS UNCHANGED. ***UPDATE TO REPORT 1258415*** THIS IS AN ONGOING INCIDENT. CALLER STATES THAT 6514 POUNDS WERE RELEASE OVER THE LAST 24 HOURS. TWO WELLS KILLED, ONE WELL WAS CAPPED AND IS FLARING, AND ONE WELL IS BLOWING OUT, NOT ON FIRE. THE TOTAL DAILY FLOW RATE REMAINS UNCHANGED. A RELIEF WELL IS PLANNED TO BE DRILLED, AND OPERATIONS ARE ONGOING. AIR MONITORING IS CONTINUING PREVIOUSLY UPDATED INFO: CALLER STATED THE RQ RELEASE OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS AT ZERO PERIODICALLY. WELL MIGHT BE REIGNITED MANUALLY FOR SAFETY AT NIGHT, BUT THEY ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY LIGHTING THEM. ALL WELLHEADS HAVE BEEN CUTOFF AND REMOVED THEREBY IMPROVING EFFICIENCY AND ABATEMENT EFFORTS. PREVIOUS REPORTS: UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1258167: CALLER STATED DEBRIS REMOVAL IS IN PROGRESS. WELLHEAD INTERVENTION IS IN PROGRESS AS WELL. THE RELEASE OF THE NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS STILL WITHIN THE REPORTABLE LEVELS BUT LESS THAN THE 13028 POUNDS LISTED IN THE PRIOR REPORT.

Report Description
PORT STAFF WAS NOTIFIED BY A TUG OWNER THAT THERE WAS A SHEEN IN THE SOUTHEAST CORNER OF THE HARBOR NEAR HIS NON-OPERATING TUGBOAT, BUT ADAMANT THAT THE SHEEN WAS OUTSIDE THE HARD BOOM AND THEREFORE NOT FROM HIS VESSEL. FACILITY WAS EXPERIENCING HIGH SOUTHERNLY WINDS AND SEAS AT THE TIME BUT SHEEN WAS TRAPPED AGAINST THE SOUTH WALL AND NOT AFFECTED BY THE WIND. PORT STAFF DEPLOYED SORBENT BOOM WITH A SKIFF TO CAPTURE MOST OF THE SHEEN AND TRAP IT AGAINST THE WALL UNTIL STORM CONDITIONS DIMINISH AND IT CAN BE RETRIEVED. STAFF SUSPECTS THE SHEEN DID ESCAPE FROM AROUND THE END OF THE TUG'S BOOM BUT IT CAN'T BE PROVEN SINCE THERE'S A STORM DRAIN IN THE SAME AREA THAT DUMPS STREET RUNOFF INTO THE HARBOR DURING RAINY PERIODS.
